title: Claims Manual: Deferred Fixed Annuities Death Benefit, Beneficiary Shares and Payout Choices
content:
Death benefit provisions of Ashgrove Deferred Fixed Annuities.

## The benefit

On the death of an owner before annuitization, the death benefit [*retired wording, no longer in force:* "is the contract value on the date due proof of death is received"] is paid with no surrender charge.

The sentence "Interest is added at the death claim interest rate, simple, for actual calendar days from the date due proof is received to payment, over 365, rounded to the cent." is **no longer in force**.

Both retired passages have been superseded by the current basis; the death claim interest rate figure itself keeps its value.

## Conditions of payment

| Condition | What the records must show |
|---|---|
| Proof and approval | Death benefit is paid only on a death claim whose certified death certificate has been received and whose request status is approved. This applies to paying the benefit, to closing the claim as paid and to a spousal continuation. |
| Contract status | Disbursement proceeds only while the contract status is death claim pending or claim paid. |

Both are read from the death claim recorded on this contract and from this contract's status, not from a caller's account.

## Who receives it

- The benefit is divided among the surviving primary beneficiaries of the designation in effect at death, by share.
- A predeceased primary beneficiary's share passes pro rata to the surviving primaries; where there are none, to the contingent beneficiaries; and where there are none of those, to the owner's estate.

## Spousal continuation

Where the tier allows spousal continuation and the owner's spouse is the sole primary beneficiary, the spouse may instead continue the contract as owner, with no restart of the surrender charge schedule, and the death benefit is not paid.

## Any other beneficiary

Any other beneficiary must take a lump sum, or apply the share to an Ashgrove income annuity beginning within the tier's beneficiary annuitization period of the date of death, or take the whole share within the tier's distribution deadline from the date of death. A share for a beneficiary younger than the tier's minor beneficiary age is paid only to a guardian or a UTMA custodian.

## Tax

The taxable part of a non-qualified death benefit is the gain over cost basis; withholding follows the partial withdrawal provisions.

## Illustrations (hypothetical)

| Designation in effect at death | Who survives the owner | Division |
|---|---|---|
| Primaries A 60%, B 40% | A and B | A 60%, B 40% |
| Primaries A 60%, B 40% | A only | A 100% (B's share passes to A) |
| Primaries A 50%, B 30%, C 20% | A and B | C's 20% passes to A and B pro rata: A 62.5%, B 37.5% |
| Primary A 100%; contingent D 100% | D only | D 100% |
| Spouse as sole primary | Spouse | The spouse may continue the contract instead of taking the benefit |

superseded_clauses: the death benefit is the contract value on the date due proof of death is received
Interest is added at death_claim_interest_rate, simple, for actual calendar days from the date due proof is received to payment, over 365, rounded to the cent.
